newsitem.title: UK: SW Trains to improve summer timetable.
newsitem.headline: SW Trains to improve summer timetable.

text.p: South West Trains, the rail franchise owned by UK transport group Stagecoach Holdings Plc, said on Tuesday that it will make more than 100 service improvements to its summer 1997 timetable.
The British railway franchise came under fire recently after it cancelled numerous services after job reductions left it with too few drivers to operate new shift patterns.
SWT said in a statement that the improvements will start on June 1. They will include some new services, service extensions, and two extra trains an hour between Reading and London Waterloo.

"The new timetable demonstrates a real growth in train services, more capacity with extra seats to ease overcrowding, and we beleive it will be welcomed by our passengers," said Brian Cox, chairman and managing director of SWT.

The franchise, which mainly operates commuter services into London, faces the possibility of a fine of one million pounds ($1.6 million) and the loss of its licence after it cancelled 2,543 trains in eight weeks.
It faces the fine if it does not meet minimum levels of services in April and May.
